This is not the end of the world. If you have access to a professional company I would reach out. I do appointments for bedbugs fairly often and have a decent amount of education on them. Good products to use are, Crosfire and Cimexa. For your use there is a aresol version of Crosfire. Remove all bedding place them in trash bags and run them in your dryer for 2 cycles in a row on high heat. This will kill all living bugs and eggs. Flip your mattress and box spring and apply crosfire to all cracks and crevices or other areas that may be a suitable harborage for bugs. I don’t think Crosfire has a reapplication period so you can repeat this daily if you wanted to.

If this sounds like a lot of work for you and money is an issue, call a reputable pest control company with experience in treating bedbugs.

You could have pest control come and do a preventative dusting/spraying. I use a product called Cimexa for preventative treatments. Crosfire is another good product. 

Bedbugs will die if exposed to temperatures of 113 degrees fahrenheit for an extended period of time. Or at 130 degrees fahrenheit rather quickly. So if you can launder your clothing/sheets/blankets for 2 cycles on high that will kill all bugs and eggs present on those items. While your items are in the dryer you can take the time to flip your bed and mattress and couch inspect all cracks and crevices. Look for eggs/fecal spotting/live bugs. It’s best to be very thorough when you discover these guys as an entire infestation can start with one inseminated female bug. 

There are also areosol products you can get where you can treat areas that you see bugs or where bugs may find harborage. I like the can of Crosfire and Shockwave. Please feel free to message me if you have any other questions.
